newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Pacific mobile plan gets T$12.6 bln loans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Pacific mobile plan gets T$12.6 bln loans.

text.p: Taiwan's Pacific Electric Wire and Cable Co Ltd has obtained T$12.6 billion in syndicated loans for its mobile phone project, lead underwriter International Commercial Bank of China said on Thursday.

"We have agreed to lead the T$12.6 billion loans, but other details have not yet finalised," a bank executive said. "More than 40 banks have said they are interested in taking part in the sydicated loans. The funds will be raised very soon."
Pacific Communications Services, led by Pacific Electric Wire and Cable, recently won the first licence for providing nationwide mobile phone services.
Other partners include shipping giant Evergreen Marine Corp, Yageo Corp, Acer Inc and GTE Corp of the United States.
Mobile telephony is one of several telecommunications sectors liberalised by Taiwan's parliament in January 1996, opening them up to private and foreign investment.
Before the reforms, telephone, data and other telecom services had been monopolised by the Directorate General of Telecommunications.
The liberalisation powered ahead on July 1, 1996 as the monopoly's operations were spun off as Chunghwa Telecommunications Corp.
